title: Didn’t Mean to Stay
pages:
If you find this, I didn’t mean to stay this long.

I told myself I’d trade, rest, then move on before dark.
That was three nights ago.

They say the Exchange is neutral.
Neutral doesn’t mean safe — it just means everyone’s watching.

If you’re reading this, don’t linger.
Nothing here stays still for long.

title: Market Rules
pages:
EXCHANGE NOTICE

• No weapons drawn
• No disputes settled on-site
• Trades are final

Violations will be remembered.
Repeated violations will be corrected.

— Syndicate Oversight

title: Supply Flow Advisory
pages:
SUPPLY FLOW ADVISORY

Stock moves fast.
If something’s available today, assume it won’t be tomorrow.

Hoarding draws attention.
Attention invites problems.

Trade smart.

title: Observation 14-C
pages:
Reclaimer Log — 14-C

Exchange traffic exceeds projection.
Despite conditions, cooperation persists.

Hypothesis: survival pressure encourages structure.
Even here.

Monitoring continues.

title: Extraction Note
pages:
Reclaimer Log — 14-F

Extraction points remain functional.
Usage suggests misunderstanding of risk.

Leaving is not escape.
It is relocation.

Reminder issued. Monitoring continues.

title: Last Route Out
pages:
Recording start…

This is Specialist Harrow, Echo-7 supply convoy.
We’re rerouting north. Main route is blocked — civilians everywhere, vehicles abandoned. Command traffic is jammed.

Corporal Daines isn’t looking good. He got scratched during the checkpoint incident. Said it was nothing.

That was three hours ago.

He stopped talking about twenty minutes back. Just… staring. Breathing slow.

I tried to wake him up. No response. Skin’s cold but he’s still breathing.

I don’t like this. I don’t like this at all.

If this recording is recovered —
Don’t let anyone ride with you if they’ve been exposed.

Daines…

…hey.

Daines?

…movement sounds…

Recording—

end signal

title: Day 12
pages:
They stopped answering on the radio this morning.
Not static. Not interference. Just silence.

I can still see the smoke columns to the south. Too many to count now. Whatever happened in the city… it wasn’t contained.

Command said hold position and observe.
So I’m observing.

The animals left first. Then the birds. Now it’s just wind and those things moving through the trees at night.

They don’t move like people anymore.

I tried signaling Tower 2 at dusk. Something moved inside the tower, but nobody answered. The lights came on for a few seconds… then went dark.

I’m not going down there.

If anyone finds this post —
Don’t wait for orders.

Orders stopped coming a long time ago.

title: OEM Training Log
pages:
OEM Training Log – Instructor Holliday

If you’re hearing this, you’re on the range. That’s good.

Out there, you don’t choose your conditions.
You don’t choose your weapon.
You don’t choose when things go wrong.

So we train for all of it.

Run every platform. Every caliber. Every configuration.

If the system spins you something unfamiliar… good.

That discomfort you feel?
That’s you learning.

Stay calm. Stay deliberate.
Slow is smooth. Smooth is fast.

— End Log

title: Day 9
pages:
Day 9

Doc says repetition builds confidence. Confidence keeps you alive.

We’ve been running the same drills for hours. Slow fire. Controlled bursts. Weapon swaps. Malfunction clears.

He doesn’t yell. Doesn’t need to.
Just watches.

First day I was here, I thought this was overkill. Too much focus on fundamentals. Too slow.

Then we lost Carter on patrol.
Weapon jammed. He panicked.
Didn’t remember the drill.

Doc didn’t say anything after we got back.
He just reset the targets and told us to start again.

I get it now.
Out there, you don’t rise to the moment.

You fall back to your training.

title: The Last Known Survivor
pages:
If you’re reading this, then either I didn’t make it back…
or you’re smarter than I was and decided to stay put for a while.

This place held longer than most.
Solid walls. Good sightlines. Water’s still clean if you boil it.

For a time, this felt like enough.

It isn’t anymore.

The storms are getting closer. The red haze hangs in the air longer after each one. Crops won’t hold. Tools fail more often. Radios only work when they feel like it.

And the Echoes…

At first it was just noise. Static. Voices where there shouldn’t be any.
Now lights turn on by themselves. Screens show things that aren’t there.

A man down the road swore he saw his family inside his house.
The house burned down three months ago.

He walked into the fire trying to reach them.

People aren’t the problem anymore.

It’s what the place is doing to them.

I heard talk from a trader passing through. Said there’s a region farther out — beyond the heavy zones.

Sigma Red hasn’t swallowed it yet.
Echo interference is rare.
Settlements still trade instead of shoot on sight.

Might be a lie. Might be wishful thinking.

But staying here isn’t working.

I’m leaving at first light.

If you find this place empty —

Don’t get comfortable.

This zone isn’t dying.

It’s changing.

title: Trophy Room
pages:
“Listen — this isn’t a trophy room.
You don’t ‘collect’ gear out here… you rotate it.

Keep your armor and supplies back in the main cabin where they’re secured.
Use this weapons cabin for the work: ammo, attachments, maintenance, swapping kits.

And don’t get cute.
The loadout you love is usually the one that gets you overconfident.”

title: MAINTENANCE LOG 9-A — POWER SURGE INCIDENT
pages:
Generator 3 nearly cooked itself again.

Something upstream fried the auxiliary relay during the last storm and the entire yard has been limping on backup power ever since. We moved remaining fuel reserves before command locked things down.

If anyone's reading this:
Generator 3 WILL NOT fully restart without:
- 2 Fuel Cells
- Auxiliary Relay Module

One fuel cell was pulled for repair and sent to the garage.
Another was relocated near training after repeated thefts from the yard.

If comms are still dead, check the tower. Last I heard, someone moved a relay upstairs after the surge.

— Chief Maintenance Tech A. Rourke

title: MECHANIC'S LOG — FUEL RATIONS FOR GENERATOR 3
pages:
Pulled one fuel cell from Generator 3 after repeated overheating reports. Planned to reinstall after diagnostics but command started evacuation before we finished.

Stored the cell near Bay 2 shelving.

Nobody touches it unless power becomes priority again.

Something keeps moving around the garage at night.

— Sgt. Mason

title: SURVEYOR'S NOTEBOOK — TRAINING SECTOR
pages:
Training grounds power has been unreliable for weeks.

Quartermaster had us move one of the emergency fuel cells into the maintenance shed after scavengers started cutting locks around the power yard.

South bunker access still feels wrong. Heat readings underground continue showing movement where there shouldn't be any.

Probably faulty sensors.

Probably.

— Survey Team Note

title: DISTRESS LOG — WATCHTOWER
pages:
Comms went dark after the surge.

Radio relay started spitting sparks before everything died. We salvaged one of the synchronization relays and stored it upstairs in case Generator 3 ever came back online.

If someone restores power:
DO NOT leave floodlights active too long.

Too much movement beyond the perimeter.

Something watches when the lights come back.

— Final Tower Entry

title: DOC-A1 — YOU PROMISED SAFETY
pages:
Dear Emma,

They told us this place was secure.

Then they stopped letting civilians leave.

Power keeps failing. Food's running low. Last night the lights went out again and something got into Barracks B. They told us it was a containment breach.

Nobody believes them anymore.

If this letter somehow makes it out:
Don't come looking for me.

— M.

title: Virelia Recruitment Poster
pages:
“Virelia”

“THE FUTURE NEEDS BUILDERS — JOIN THE CONTAINMENT INITIATIVE TODAY!”

“We built our own grave.”

title: News Bulletin #42
pages:
“Breaking: Virelia announces temporary suspension of civilian supply routes.
Citizens urged to remain indoors. Rumors of ‘Catalyst anomalies’ are baseless and unpatriotic.”

title: The Marauder Manifesto
pages:
“There’s no more government. No more gods. Only the hungry.”

“We take what we can, when we can.
The Exchange hoards. The Reclaimers preach. The Agency hides.
But we? We live.”

“If you hear the drums past midnight, run.
They’re not warning shots — they’re dinner bells.”

title: Letter to a Dead Brother
pages:
“Evan,
I burned your dog tags today. Thought it would set you free.
Instead, the smoke curled into shapes that spoke your name.
I followed them to the bridge, and the wind was full of voices I knew.
If you come back tonight… don’t knock.
I don’t want to see what’s left of you.”

title: Letter to My Son
pages:
“Lukas —

If you find this, I’m sorry. The storms came early this year. I left the farm to trade with the Syndicate for seed packs, but they never came.

The cold gets in your bones here. Makes you forget faces. Makes you think the wind’s whispering your name.

I still plant every spring. I still keep your mother’s greenhouse running with the last of the power cells.

Maybe one day you’ll come home and see green again.
Maybe.”

title: Handwritten Note
pages:
“They say you can hear the Core if you hold still long enough.
I did.
It doesn’t beat like a heart.
It breathes.”

title: The Hunter
pages:
“Day 182. Wolves took the last deer three nights ago.
Tried fishing — the water froze around the line.

Built a snare trap. Caught something that wasn’t an animal. It had fingers.

I buried it, but it keeps scratching from under the ice.”

title: Structural Log: Depth-7
pages:
“The frost is eating the weld seams again.
I hear it breathing through the steel — slow, like lungs under snow.
Core pulses steady at six-minute intervals. It isn’t interference. It’s… listening.

I told Kovak we should power down for recalibration. She smiled, said it was learning restraint.”

title: The Extractor’s First Night
pages:
“They said it would just be a recon run — grab a crate, mark the route, head back by dawn.
But dawn doesn’t exist here. The snow glows blue at night, and the wind screams like something trapped in the ice.

I met a man near the bridge — or what’s left of him. Said his name was ‘Rook.’ Wore Agency armor, eyes gone black. He told me to stay out of the tunnels.
Then he walked into the storm.

I don’t know if he was real.
My radio picks up a heartbeat every six minutes.”

title: Black Box
pages:
“—Containment breach! They’re not dying, they’re getting back up—”

[Screams / rifle burst / static]
“Kovak said it would stabilize— she lied! It’s feeding off the dead!”

[Something drags across metal — wet breathing]
“Borén, if you hear this… seal it. Seal everything—”

title: Kovak’s Private Log 17
pages:
“We didn’t create life. We disturbed death.
The Core echoes every organism it’s touched, and it’s begun to whisper back.

I can hear them through the vents — the test subjects. They shouldn’t still have voices.”

title: Dr. Vanya Kirov — Private Audio Memo #6
pages:
“The storms grow stronger every cycle. The Core’s pulses are accelerating.
I can feel it in my bones now — a rhythm that doesn’t belong to the living.
If Elena’s still down there, she’s part of its song now.

I’m beginning to think we were never scientists.
Just gravediggers with clipboards.”

title: Internal Email Chain — VCI Legal Department
pages:
From: R. Kelner (Compliance Chief)
To: All Division Leads

“Public relations requests we avoid terms like ‘mutation,’ ‘infection,’ and ‘corpse resonance.’
Replace with ‘adaptive response’ or ‘bio-optimization event.’ Stay positive!”

title: Reclaimer Field Notes #22
pages:
“Core radiation defies thermodynamics. Temperatures below zero yet readings spike positive.
Energy flows inward, not outward — like it’s feeding something buried.

It isn’t a reactor. It’s a womb. And something inside it is remembering hunger.”

title: Reclaimer Intercept — Encrypted Transmission
pages:
Date: 2117.08.12 
“Vanya, they’re going to bury her under the ice and call it salvation.
The Core’s heartbeat matches hers exactly — that’s no accident.
If we can stabilize its rhythm, we save the world. If we can’t, the world was never worth saving.”

title: Reclaimer Field Diary – Lt. Col. Emil Borén
pages:
“We built this span for connection, not conquest.
The day it fell, I understood — bridges only matter when someone’s left on the other side.”

title: The Final Broadcast
pages:
“If anyone’s still alive… listen.
The Core is learning. It’s using the dead as language.
Don’t follow the heartbeat — it’s not calling you, it’s calling them.”
